parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *ludraz (“useless; worthless; bad”), according to Pokorny, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leut-, from *(s)lew- (“slack, loose, limp, flabby”). Compare Old English loddere, Old High German lotar (“vain; void; insignificant”), Middle High German lotter. See also
Likely a calque of Middle High German welhisch nuz, from Proto-Germanic *walhaz (“foreign”) + *hnuts (“nut”). Cognate of Polish orzech włoski.
